question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $4x+9\ge 1$ and $1-3x>7.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $4x+9\ge 1\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+9 & \ge 1 \\ 4x+9-9 & \ge 1-9 \\ 4x & \ge -8 \\ \frac{4x}{4} & \ge \frac{-8}{4} \\ x & \ge -2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/1673c69df6497fd90ddab9c51c208ca5110f0e3c5a03a101e3b46723e04081fe.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $1-3x>7\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-3x & >7 \\ 1-3x-1 & >7-1 \\ -3x & >6 \\ (-1)\cdot (-3x) & <(-1)\cdot 6 \\ 3x & <-6 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & <\frac{-6}{3} \\ x & <-2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/b97b78ec613e826f7f8beb7336d3c2f285fc58d9bbf0c0f9d59921f41de2b3b6.png)

$$

$$

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/544d23551ed218c0d7e373ba0d04dbe1ad51d587c452b875c1a45df2e896cd87.png)

$$

$$

It turns out that the solutions do not overlap at all. Therefore, there are no values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities simultaneously. So, there is no solution.
